title: Edit Distance
statement:
The edit distance (Levenshtein distance) between two strings A and B is the minimum number of single-character operations needed to transform A into B.

Allowed operations:
1. Insert a character.
2. Delete a character.
3. Replace a character with another.

Given strings A and B, compute their edit distance.
constraints:
0 <= |A|, |B| <= 1000
A and B contain only lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: Two lines: the first contains A, the second contains B.
outputFormat: A single integer: the edit distance between A and B.

starterCode.python:
a = input().strip()
b = input().strip()
